utterances.text: Since we are colleagues, we share the same profession. You graduated from the University of Sarajevo in 1982. Actually, you graduated from its department in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English transcript, it says "in 1982," and in the French interpretation, I heard "1992." Can you clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in 1982.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up to 1990, you worked as a lawyer in a company. You were in charge of the application drafting an implementation of legal acts of that company.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: No, that was not all. I also represented my company before court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you drafted the legal enactments. You applied law. You implemented those legal enactments. And you represented the legal interests of your company. And this was your experience up to then.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, up to then, that was my experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1990, the first multi-party elections were held in Bosnia and Herzegovina. After the elections, in February 1990 -- 1991, you were appointed the Secretary of the Secretariat for the National Defence of Travnik Municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. However, I was first transferred to the municipality as the head of the military department, which is a part of the secretariat. It was on the 4th of October, 1990, before the multi-party elections were held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were an employee of the Secretariat of the National Defence which was the municipal Ministry for Defence, from the year 1990. And then you were appointed its secretary; or in other words, the Ministry of the Secretariat for Defence in February 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although this was a defence organ, which functioned at the level of Travnik municipality, your secretariat, as a matter of fact, was a state organ and it was an integral part of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You actually held two positions: One of your positions was subordinated to the Ministry of Bosnia and Herzegovina; and your second link was with the executive board or the administration of Travnik municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that would be correct later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to the law, you were also a member of the executive board of the municipality by virtue of your position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A similar legal position was also held by the Secretariat for the Interior Affairs or -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that. I don't know whether that secretariat occupied the same position as my secretariat, whether it had the same role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Secretariat for National Defence belonged to the civilian structure rather than to the military structure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. This was a link between the civilian and military authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your secretariat at that time, from 1991 onwards, for as long as you were its member, consisted of three departments: The military department that discharged duties pertaining to the scope of defence; the civilian department which executed duties belonging to the civilian defence; and the department for monitoring and surveillance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The military department that you had belonged to before becoming the head of the secretariat was in charge of the mobilisation of able-bodied men and also kept track of the able-bodied men who were older than 18.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, all the able-bodied men up to the age of 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once a person is 18, they become conscripts and the military department sends them call-up papers for the compulsory military service.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the compulsory military service, these people were then assigned to reserve military duties as reserve members of the Yugoslav People's Army, the reserve members of the Territorial Defence, reserve members of the police, or those who had work obligation within their respective companies and those who were assigned to various duties in the civilian protection; is that more or less the way, how you kept a record of military conscripts in your secretariat?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is more or less the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to that, the military department of your secretariat also had a duty and obligation to look after the logistics in case of war and in case of natural disasters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the former SFRY and in Bosnia-Herzegovina all the way up to the war, in addition to the Yugoslav People's Army the only military structure was the Territorial Defence which had its command structure; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, the commander of the Territorial Defence was elected - that is, the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina - was elected by the Assembly of the Republic and the Territorial Defence of the Municipality was -- the commander of the Territorial Defence in the municipality was elected by the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't know what period you're referring to. There are two periods; before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know better. I'm not that familiar with the issue, but I believe that the commander of the Territorial Defence had to be confirmed by the municipal assembly.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: You are right. But when you're talking about two periods. I'm talking about the period while the SFRY still existed and the second period is the period once Bosnia-Herzegovina proclaimed its independence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Thank you. In the former SFRY, you have just reminded me, in case of war the Territorial Defence was duty-bound to subordinate itself to the Yugoslav People's Army, to its command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that sometime at the beginning of 1990, before the multi-party elections, the former SFRY passed a decision according to which all the weapons in the possession of the Territorial Defence should be placed under the control of the Yugoslav People's Army? This was later abused and these arms were turned against Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't be sure of that. However, I know that the weapons that belonged to the Territorial Defence was kept in special warehouses which were guarded by the regular JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In case of war, the reserve police and the civilian protection, the Department for Surveillance and Monitoring were placed under civilian structures, whereas the Territorial Defence was a military structure. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Rajic, that throughout all this time while you were in Travnik and after the beginning of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina not for a moment in the municipality military authorities were set up? The civilian authorities carried out its duties and the military structures carried out their duties.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. There was a bit of overlapping and interference, if we are talking about these structures. I am not talking about the JNA -- the JNA was not involved -- but the Territorial Defence and some other units and formations which already existed and which had not been under the strength of the organisation of military structures in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you're saying is that after the beginning of the war, given the role the municipal and political structures played in the municipalities, that they still had a significant influence over the military structures. Would I be correct in saying that their influence sometimes even prevailed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: In case of war or imminent danger of war, the civilian structures at the time -- the municipal assembly no longer carried out its role. According to the law on the National Defence of the former Yugoslavia which was in effect in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the War Presidency of the municipality was set up. Under such conditions, the War Presidency took over the role of the municipal assembly, the political structures, and others. This was prescribed by the law. The War Presidency was headed by the president of the municipal assembly, according to the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on and let's explain some things that preceded the war. Is it true that on the 6th of April, 1992, Bosnia and Herzegovina was internationally recognised as a state?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on that same day the JNA and the Serbian forces attacked Sarajevo and that this was the beginning of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Sarajevo did come under attack. It had already been blocked. But I don't think that this was the beginning of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The war started with the attack on Ravno village, certain events in Bijeljina, and so on. However, the official attack on the capital meant that the war was going on.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I cannot agree with that. For me the war started before that. It was going on at the time; however, it was still going on in 1993 as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, would you agree with me if I said that Bosnia and Herzegovina, as a matter of fact, was the only known state which on the day when it proclaimed its independence was attacked and in its struggle for independence it started creating its armed forces? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: No, I can't agree with that, because when we are talking about Bosnia and Herzegovina -- I voted in the referendum and voted for the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was my homeland. However, up to then -- that's why I can't agree with you about the beginning of the war. Up to then there had already been some preparations for war and this was obvious. It started with Slovenia. It moved down to Croatia and then arrived in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In Travnik, both sides and the third side even before that - I'm talk about Bosniaks, Serbs, and Croats - started organising themselves because it was already clear that at that moment unity was not going to be useful to any of them. And that is why I am saying that the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is, of Bosnia-Herzegovina, started being created even before that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. And now we as lawyers, can we agree about some facts? Is it true that on the 8th of April, 1992, after the JNA attacked Sarajevo, the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as the legitimate body of that state, proclaimed the imminent threat of war? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe that this was when the imminent state of war was proclaimed. I can't be sure of the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Presidency on the same day reached the decision according to which the Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was proclaimed as the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Rajic, that in May 1992 the Presidency approved a legal provision about defence and about the military and the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina according to which they were proclaimed to be the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that claim.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to witness to be shown the text of the above-mentioned provision -- we have enough copies to go around -- so that the witness may be reminded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm turning to the Defence. Before you ask the question, could you indicate to the Trial Chamber what is the point of this question about context.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness was secretary for the Territorial Defence of the Municipality of Travnik. These are the legal documents, some of which we got from the Prosecution in relation to the expert-witness account, and others are documents pertaining to other cases. These are the basic defence documents about the defence and the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. My client is a commander in the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I would like to put a couple of questions to the witness in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, first of all, we haven't received copies of the document that will be shown to the witness. And in respect to the last question of my learned colleague, I wish to draw the attention of both Defence and the Trial Chamber to paragraph 4 of the Annex to the Third Amended Indictment, in which is written: "On 20 May 1992, the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina passed the decree on the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina which formally established the ABiH." As the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution cannot see the relevance of the questions put to this witness, since the answers the Defence will find in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is an act which is either proven or argued against. If it is useful for the Prosecution to do that, I don't see the point of this complaint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. You can continue with your cross-examination of the witness on the basis of the document dated the 20th of May, 1992, which is a very official document. It can't get more official than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question to the witness is this: As the secretary for the Territorial Defence -- basically the Minister of Defence for the Municipality of Travnik -- was he aware of the fact that the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina had approved a law, had passed a law, about the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I was not aware of it. I have never set eyes on this document. At the time when this provision was approved, I was no longer the Secretary for the Territorial Defence. I was, formally speaking, legally speaking, because I had been the only elected person; but I no longer worked and did any work for the Secretariat of the Territorial Defence and I had no power over the members of the Bosniak nationality. And this is dated the 15th of November, 1992, and it is very questionable as to whether my colleagues, Bosniaks, had been given this paper. I mean, this is just something I suppose. I'm not going to go into this. But I'd like to let you know why I was no longer a secretary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean, were you relieved of your duties?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I had never been relieved of my duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says underneath that it was published in the official journal number 4, 1992, and at the end of the provision there is the date of publication. But the date of the 15th of November is the date when, in the special OJ of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the same provision was published again. It was approved in May and published in May 1992. This is just for clarification. And I'm asking you, in case you did not see this text yourself, okay, this is your answer. And due to the relevance of this document, I would like to Trial Chamber to accept it as a submission from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. This text indicates that it was created on the 14th of May, 1992. It was signed by President Izetbegovic. It is indicated here. And that Article 139 indicates that this decree with a force of law refers to the defence, and it will be published in the OJ of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So it is an official document. And so we can't object to you tendering or submitting a document which was drawn up by a legal authority. So you are tendering this document in B/C/S plus an English translation; is that correct? All right. Mr. Registrar, give me a B/C/S number and a number for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S version will get the exhibit number DH29; and the English translation will get the exhibit number DH29/E.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like the witness to be shown another decree with the force of law, and it is the decree which refers to the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Once again, we've got enough copies for everyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, are you aware of the fact that the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 20th of May, 1992 passed a decree with a force of law about the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. And in order for me to have been aware of it, I would have had to receive a copy of the official journal of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I did not get that. And I'm not aware of this. And this, once again, is a copy of the text. I would like to see an official journal of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not the official journal of the Armed Forces of BH, because only the provisions -- as you know full well -- published in the official journal or Official Gazette, whatever it was called at the time, were published -- considered to have been published on the day of publication. But as I was saying, I never got to see this and I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, for the purpose of clarification, since the Prosecution referred to the Official Gazette of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina which put together a number of decrees and legal documents from the military field, in this document too you can see that this decree too was published in the official journal of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina for 1992 -- in May 1992. And here it is repeated once again, it is being published once again in the Official Gazette of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This is for the sake of clarification and for the sake of the transcript. And you did say that you did not get to see the text of this provision. Did you find out about it through the media, the radio, for example? Did you find out about the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina being set up?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I think -- I had heard -- I don't think. I did hear about it. But when exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wanted to intervene at this stage. The Defence has produced an English translation of a decree which was published in the Official Gazette of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And we have a B/C/S document which apparently reproduces in full the text of the articles, since in the English text we have 43 articles; in the B/C/S text, we also have 43 articles, so apparently it's the same text. But the witness, who is a law graduate as well, is stressing that the B/C/S text is taken from a document of the armed forces, and indeed my knowledge of the B/C/S language is not quite sufficient, but I can see on top of this page the words "Sluzbeni List, Armije BiH." I suppose that it is a reference to a military type of document and the witness is saying this is a military text. In order to give an opinion, he would have had to see a copy of the official journal. Now, the translation is based on the military text or on the text published in the OJ? Because in the English translation, you have a reference to this Official Gazette and not the military text.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, for the sake of clarification, the Prosecution has submitted this text along with the translation into English to us, plus all the other documents for General Reinhardt, and it is a translation based on the OJ published on the 20th of May, 1992. The Prosecution did not enclose to that document the BH translation of the text [as interpreted], and this is the reason why we used the same text as it was published in the official journal of the armed forces several months later. This is the difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Now it is much more clear, and it will be recorded in the transcript. Now, following a question from the Defence and an answer from the witness and a question put to the witness -- and a question put by the Trial Chamber, it appears now that the English text, which was submitted by the Prosecution - and there is a number which does establish that this is a text coming from the Prosecution - is the text which was translated from the B/C/S. It would have been better if the Prosecution had at the same time given the B/C/S version of the text to the Defence, since the Defence did not have the original text in the B/C/S, looked into the army documents and came up with this decree in the B/C/S language. So that's the explanation of this mystery; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the witness, who is an eminent legal expert, has noticed straight away that there was a difference between the two documents, to the extent that the B/C/S text was coming from the army; whereas, the English text was coming from the Prosecution and was a translation based on the official journal. But what I believe is the most important thing is for the 43 articles to be included in both texts. You may continue, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, is it correct that Article 2 of this provision establishes that the armed forces of the republic, made up of the armed forces of the republic, thereafter army, and then the police and the armed units coming under the unified command of the armed forces of the republic? Is that the provision of the armed forces of the republic?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: That's what it says in the text, but I can't tell you whether it really happened. It says so in the text, but you know full well that that was not the situation reflected on the ground. This could not have been implemented on the ground, because Bosnia and Herzegovina was made up of three peoples. It was a uniform -- unified territory. And in order for this to apply, in order for your claim to apply, this would have had to apply throughout the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I ask you not to get away from the topic.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in the text. But one can write whatever one likes, if it has no bearing on the real situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's come back to your question. Is it correct that the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina up until the war and even later guaranteed full equality and constitutional rights for all peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina: Serbs, Croats, and Muslims, Bosniaks? Is that correct? Is it correct that it was all enshrined in the Constitution?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was indeed enshrined in the Constitution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also correct that all the institutions at the level of the republic and the municipality were made up of members of all peoples, nationalities? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: In those places in which there was multi-ethnic population, it was indeed the case. The members of all the peoples living in that given territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the multi-party elections in 1990, the multi-ethnic make-up of the municipalities continued to exist, except that new people have come to power with new political agendas?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: That was the case in Travnik, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And right before the war, the political allegiance of the authorities in Travnik changed, but the national structure, the national make-up, including members of all nationalities remained the same; is that true?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, it lasted for a very short time after the elections, because - and I'm referring to Travnik now - because the representatives of the Serb people who were carrying out certain political and executive duties left those authorities and withdrew, basically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was precisely what I was going to ask you about. Is it indeed true that in the beginning of 1992 the elected officials, members of the SDS party, left there -- their jobs in the municipality and set up their own separate power structure or simply left?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in the -- within the authorities, we had certain members of the Serb population, not members of the nationalist parties, but there were much -- there were fewer of them. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether any members of the Serb nation remained in any official positions of power. But as to people working in clerical positions for the municipality, within administrations, yes; but they did not have any position of power or responsibility. Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that once these SDS representatives withdrew in the joint institutions, Croats and Muslims continued to work together?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, after the departure of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier on, you said that in the municipality, in line with the legal provisions, the War Presidency was set up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but prior to the departure of the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleagues are telling me that maybe I've missed it. Perhaps the law on the armed forces should be tendered as a document from the Defence. I just wouldn't like to forget. So perhaps it would be appropriate for us to do so before the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means. On the other hand, as we are dealing with all these legal matters at the moment, this decree, this legal decree, which is based apparently on one article, para 3 of the Constitution -- I mean, we don't have the text of the Constitution here, and we don't have the amendment either. Perhaps at a later stage you'll get the opportunity to submit those texts as well. But as you know, there is a certain hierarchy when it comes to the legal documents. If there is a reference to a legal document in another text, you have to have the original text as well, and I don't see it here. On the other hand, this legal decree is signed by Mr. Izetbegovic, but it followed the recommendation submitted by the government. And apparently the Presidency had the competence to approve this legal decree. But we would really like to see the text of the constitutional document. Certainly it will be submitted on another occasion. Now, Mr. Registrar, the Defence is asking us for the English text to be tendered. It is a translation from -- of the text from the OJ of the BH Republic and the document coming from the armed forces, and it refers to the same text. Do please give us a number now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S text will get the exhibit number DH30; and the English translation will get the exhibit number DH30/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. It is twenty to 6.00, so we'd better have a break now and we'll continue at five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. We can continue with the hearing as soon as everybody's here again. All right, then. We have about an hour left.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, just one more question in conjunction with these laws: Can you tell me if it is correct that at the time when these laws were approved - that is to say, the first half of 1992 - the defence minister of Bosnia and Herzegovina was Mr. Jerko Doko? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I know that he was a minister in 1991. As to for how long in 1992 or later, I don't know. I don't know until what time exactly and I don't know whether in the period of time that you're referring to he was indeed a minister or not. He might have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jerko Doko is a Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you. Now I would like to ask you to talk to me about a number of points that you did talk about with my learned colleague from the Prosecution. You said that already by the middle of 1992 or in the summer of 1992 in Travnik you noticed that some foreigners were coming. And I'm going to paraphrase what you said - from the Middle East, from the Middle Eastern countries, that is to say, the Northern African countries. The Middle East, the African countries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can remember, he did not mention Northern Africa.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He mentioned Egypt and so on, so I thought Egypt was in the north of Africa, so that's why I said I'm going to paraphrase your statement. I didn't quote the witness, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But yes. To simplify things, you noticed some people coming from the Arab countries; is that so?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: It is more or less so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that they came with various humanitarian organisations and that those humanitarian organisations had their premises in different places in Travnik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I think that they came through the humanitarian organisations because I saw them in those areas and on the premises rented by the humanitarian organisations of the Arab countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that they most often could be seen in the company of the representatives of those humanitarian organisations and the representatives and persons belonging to the religious life of Travnik? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Look, I don't know whether they could be seen with the representatives of those international humanitarian organisations, because I don't know who the representatives of those humanitarian organisations were. But I saw those people in the area where they had those offices. But as to contacts, as to whether they were in touch with the representatives of the religion or whatever, yes, I did see them in the company with -- in the company of various representatives of the Muslim nation in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also in reply to a question put to you by the Prosecution, you answered that they probably obtained arms in different ways. My question is this: Is it correct that at that time, in the beginning of the war in 1992, both in Travnik and in the wider area there was a very active black market for arms and weapons? Under various different circumstances and conditions people were trying to buy arms? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I think that there was a black market for arms. But as to whether it was legal -- I mean, it was a black market in fact. It was smuggling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're aware of the fact that those people -- the Arabs, I mean -- would come with the money and they too were able to purchase arms on that black market? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, not only that they could, but I heard it being said that they did indeed buy and that they had the money for those purchases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Rajic, that at the same time - that is to say, between April and May 1992 and then throughout the year, and especially after the fall of Jajce - tens of thousands of displaced persons, having been chased away from Bosanska Krajina, arrived in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. And according to my knowledge - and my impressions were based on what was said by the official representatives in Travnik at the time - about 120.000 people came through Travnik and some of them stayed there. Most of them were Muslims. The overwhelming majority were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that those displaced persons came or stayed or transitted through Travnik and they had no property, no personal belongings, nothing at all, because they had been chased away from their houses, from their homes? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. Those were poor people. Because I myself was one of them later on. In -- exactly the same as those people, and I had organised some sort of assistance for them earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the fall of Jajce and after the withdrawal of the armed forces from that area there were individuals or groups of people coming to Travnik and they were carrying arms?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at that time - that is to say, by the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993 - the army tried to get those people mobilised and get them under the army control?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Not only the people from Jajce, but also the earlier refugees from Bosanska Krajina who had come to the area. And that was before the fall of Jajce. In the meantime, the 17th Krajiska Brigade was already stationed in Travnik and they recruited able-bodied men out of those groups chased away by Serb armed forces from the area of Bosanska Krajina. And I believe that every man had some sort of war schedule assigned to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that together with these refugees new institutions of power were being set up, Okruglo [phoen], Banja Luka, the War Presidency of the Kotor Varos municipality, and they were trying to make an impact and exert influence over this part of the displaced population?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was then when they arrived, but the bodies that you referred to just now, well, I heard about them after the hostilities between the Bosnian armed forces and the HVO were suspended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your replies to my earlier questions -- you have actually answered this -- but before the beginning of the war there were preparations being made for the war in Travnik as well. Is it correct that at that time the preparations were being made under the influence and in the organisation of the political parties rather than the actual official authorities; that is to say, your secretariats? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is the case. Nothing was obtained through the secretariat, save for the things that I did as the secretary. I managed to obtain some 20 short-barrelled rifles from the depot of the Territorial Defence, and also in Travnik we managed to obtain and distribute arms to the reserve force of the police. We're talking about 400 long-barrel rifles. But this is all small arms, infantry arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So some units are formed by both peoples, apart from the legal bodies of authorities. Is it true that Bosnia-Herzegovina, which on the 22nd of May, just like the Republic of Croatia was admitted in the United Nations, was still the only internationally recognised state in the area?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: The fact is that Bosnia-Herzegovina was the only internationally recognised state in that area within the borders of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up to the end of the war, there were no other elections which would replace the government elected in 1992. The first elections after the war took place after the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as the elections are concerned. However, in Travnik everything was changed even without the elections. The president of the municipal assembly was replaced. Instead of Izet Tamuric, who is a Bosniak, Muhamed Curic was elected as president. I'm talking about top positions, but the same applied to other positions. So the ones who were elected in the first elections no longer represented any relevant force that anybody would obey or respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answering one of my previous questions, you said that Sarajevo had been completely blocked from the 2nd of May, 1992. You didn't mention the date; I have just added that. And for that reason, there was practically no communication with Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, I did not have any communication with Sarajevo at all. Only from time to time I would be able to listen to the news at 10.00, and that was the only thing that I could listen to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Rajic, that Travnik, as well as in the entire Central Bosnia, depended on the freedom of communication with the borders with the Republic of Croatia so that it was -- one possibility was Busovaca and Kiseljak, and other possibility was Gornji Vakuf and Kiseljak, and further on via Western Bosnia towards the Republic of Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. However, this communication was not via the main roads. This communication, most of it was via -- or across the mountains, across Rostovo, as you go towards Gornji Vakuf or across Vrana, if you move further on. You couldn't use the main roads that still exist because the main roads -- the traffic on the main roads was interrupted in Kupres and in other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This interruption was due to the fact that these places were temporarily occupied by the Serbian forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That was precisely the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the usher to show the witness two maps. We have enough copies for all the parties in the courtroom. We would like to use these maps to illustrate what is being said in the courtroom for all the parties in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect, I know that my friend had a lot of latitude in cross-examination, but where -- where is this taking us? And how does this tie in with what is -- what was -- how does it relate to the evidence that was led by the witness in examination-in-chief? I am totally at a loss. And perhaps with some guidance from the Court, we could probably get back on track.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have just asked questions which are directly related to the situation in Travnik. And now I'm moving on and asking questions of general interest because the witness has just told me that communication is one of the major issues that had an impact on the situation in the area. I would like to show the Trial Chamber the illustration of the situation that Travnik and the whole general area was in at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. In any case, there is no need to put forth any objections to the map, once the map is presented. Any map is just going to enable us to be better acquainted with the whole situation and to see where Travnik is. So we have two documents. Which one do you want to see first?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like the witness to recognise both, because we will be coming back to the same questions with other witnesses as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to the witness is as follows: Do you recognise the borders of any of the republics in any of these two maps? The one that you recognise, can you please put it on the ELMO so that we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the transcript, are you saying that these borders are the borders of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that these are the borders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us: The sign in the middle, does it approximately depict the area that we know as Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't stretch as far as Sarajevo. And maybe it is too close to Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, then. Thank you. We have heard the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this map into evidence. We want to have a map of Bosnia-Herzegovina as part of the evidence in this case. The second map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Can we give an exhibit number to this document. The first map with the borders of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Mr. Registrar, can we have a number for the first map that we have seen on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first map showing the whole Bosnia and Herzegovina will get the exhibit number DH31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, can you please pay attention to the roads, because my previous question was about the roads and about communication. Is it true that the main road towards the sea went from Bosanski Brod via Zenica, Visoko, and Sarajevo and further down towards Konjic and Mostar, and its exit to the sea was in the Republic of Croatia? Was that the main road in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: This is a very small scale, so I don't know whether this -- these are roads or these are river streams. As far as I can see it here, this is the Neretva, the Bosna, the Lasva, and the Vrbas Rivers. So in this map it is very hard to tell and answer your question. However, it is true that the road from the north to the south of Bosnia and Herzegovina did follow the flow of the Bosna River and then the Neretva River down to the sea.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my learned friend is on his feet. I'm going to withdraw my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution noticed a number of times - and I think now it's the time to raise it - that whenever Defence tries to tender a map there was never ever a scale on the map. This is only one issue. However, the Defence wishes this witness to comment on the roads which are detailed on this map. The Defence, may it please inform the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution of the -- whether the maps -- whether the roads on this map mirror the situation of the relevant time frame; namely, 1993. The Prosecution nor -- neither the Prosecution nor the Trial Chamber is in any position to say or to evaluate whether the roads detailed on this map were the roads in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I'm not receiving an interpretation -- no, I am receiving the interpretation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Prosecution says that there's no scale on the map. We don't know what the scale of the map is. And secondly, when it comes to roads, since we do not have a scale, we cannot be able to tell what the length of the roads is. In addition to that, the witness cannot answer your question because he says that -- that these might be river flows rather than roads. And I am in the same position. So we have a problem identifying features on your map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in addition to that, something that has just been pointed to me by my fellow Judge, we don't know whether this map dates from the year 1993 or this is a current map that was drawn this year. So we don't have the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the witness said that he cannot speak about the map, I withdrew my question. So all other discussion is pointless. So I am withdrawing my motion for this map to be tendered into evidence. So I withdraw my question and I withdraw the motion to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're withdrawing the second map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the first map, you are not withdrawing that. You want this to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then, thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, let's go back to some questions that pertain to your job. And you said that the situation on the ground was different. Once the general mobilisation was proclaimed, in your Secretariat for National Defence in Travnik you carried out mobilisation of the population into the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Only partly. However, it is not completely true, because at that time I was no longer the secretary. I was the secretary formally, on paper, but I could not influence the situation on the ground. I was in charge for the replenishment of the HVO units and Bosniaks who worked with me, my colleagues, they were in charge of the replenishment of the Territorial Defence and other units, because it was -- there was not just the Territorial Defence. There were also other units. In order to clarify things for you, at that time I could not send call-up papers to a member of the Bosniak people. I could not mobilise Bosniak people into a unit that was predominantly a Bosniak unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only mobilised the able-bodied Croats, for the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Only partly, because the units themselves also were in charge of their replenishment. It was not just the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now be shown a document that we have in both -- in English, French, and in B/C/S. This document has been located by the Defence in the Kordic case. In the Kordic case, it was a Prosecution exhibit. At the same time, I would like the witness to be shown another document which is the same document published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. We have this only in B/C/S and in English. We have enough copies for all the parties in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, is this the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna which was passed on the 18th of November, 1991? Later on this was published in the Official Gazette of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna in September 1992.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the decision. However, I see it for the first time. At that time, representatives of the political parties were involved, and I was not a member of the HDZ at the time. I only joined in 1992 or 1993. I don't know exactly. So I was not present at any of the meetings. I am aware of the fact that this decision was published in the Official Gazette. However, I have never seen this decision before in the form presented to me today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw it when it was published in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is true, but I was aware of its existence even before. However, I was not aware of who the people were who were informed in the proclamation of this community.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness has been given a copy of the decision from the Official Gazette - it's the same wording; the only difference is the list of the persons who were present when the decision was being adopted - so I would like to tender both documents as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President -- Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Although - and I really emphasise that - although the fact that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna proclaimed its existence on the 18th of November, 1991, is detailed in paragraph 5 of the Annex to the Third Amended Indictment, as a matter of principle the Prosecution objects against tendering this document into evidence. The witness has clearly answered that he wasn't at any point in time involved in rendering this decision. The witness was only saying yes, it has been published in the Official Gazette. It's an official document; of course it has been published in the Official Gazette. The witness cannot contribute and cannot add anything to this document. The Prosecution objects against tendering this document into evidence, as a matter of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me that the witness has said that he never saw this document in this form. He never read it, he never saw it. However, he did say that he was aware of its existence. Witness, this text is a decision, the decision on the establishment of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. You said that you did not read it before; however, it seems to me that you have told us that you were aware of its existence. You knew that this decision had been passed. Can you please tell us something more about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time I received the text was one year after the proclamation, and then I became aware of what it says in this text. I know people from Travnik who went and were involved. I know that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that the text which was published in November 1991, you only saw it a year later, in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was towards the end of 1992, because you can see that this Official Gazette was published in September 1992. It was only after that date that I was able to read this text, because it was only after that that I could lay my hands on this document; not before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that you did read this text at the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After this clarification provided by the witness, does the Prosecution still claim that the witness was not aware of the document? Although, the witness has just told us that he became aware of the document towards the end of 1992, which precedes the time relevant for the indictment. Can the Prosecution tell us something about that? I would like to remind you that in the indictment the establishment of this community is specifically mentioned. "On the 18th of November, 1991," it says in the indictment, "the political, cultural, economic and territorial entity within Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," and so on and so forth. So this is specifically mentioned in the indictment. And the witness has told us that he was aware of the document. He got to read it towards the end of 1992. The time relevant to the indictment is the period from April to January 1992. Is the Prosecution still opposed to these two documents being admitted? Are you still objecting to that, Mr. Withopf? The witness has told us that towards the end of 1992 he was aware of the existence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: That's exactly the point, Mr. President, Your Honours. What's the evidential value of a document that only proves or is supposed to prove what's written in the indictment? I don't see any need to tender anything into evidence what is written in the indictment, and the witness is not in a position to add anything to the fact that is pleaded in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We shall withdraw to deliberate. Can you please remain in the courtroom. We will be back shortly. --- Break taken at 6.42 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing can continue. The Trial Chamber allows for this document to be tendered, to the extent that the constitution of that community is referred to specifically in the indictment, and it sets to illustrate the overall military context and political context at the time. So we will attribute a number to, this because we've got two sets of documents. Mr. Registrar, so we've got one document, B/C/S, in English, and in French. So we need a number, and the three references.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH32 for the B/C/S version of the decision; DH32/E for the English version; and DH32/F for the French version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. And the second document: Because we've got a second document which is B/C/S and the translation into English. The reference is 00311937, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S version gets the exhibit number DH33; and the English translation gets the exhibit number DH33/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Could the Defence continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to tell you straight away that I believe I will be unable to complete the cross-examination of the witness by 7.00. So do please have some understanding for this, because we believe that this is a witness who had an important position in the municipality of Travnik and who can make a major contribution to establishing the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that we shall have to continue tomorrow. All right, then. Witness, you will have understood that there is a problem. You'll have to come back tomorrow morning. There's no problem for you, specifically.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We shall continue until 7.00, and then we'll stop at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to look at this decision from the OJ that in his capacity -- in his job in Travnik he must have received. I would just like to put a couple of questions to him in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Article 2 of these basic provisions, it is indicated what municipalities make up the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the municipalities of Jajce, Travnik, Fojnica, Kakanj, Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Konjic, Jablanica, Mostar, and Stolac are on that list; and these are towns in which, according to the census of 1991, the majority population was Bosniak and Muslim, whether we were talking about the absolute majority or relative majority?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that what you're saying is correct. I have a list -- but not here -- a list with the census data in BH, and if I were able to consult that, I could tell you. But I really don't know the population make-up of all these municipalities you've listed here. In Travnik, yes, there was a relative majority for Muslims and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that on the basis of this decision, all Lasva Valley communities are here, Lasva, Vitez, Busovaca, Travnik and Nova Travnik, as well as the other municipalities in central Bosnia, Gornji Vakuf and Bugojno? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: What you're saying is correct. This article encompasses those municipalities. But it's not really true, because some of them, which are not covered, were from that area that you're referring to, Central Bosnia, and they're not listed here. And -- I do apologise. And they were -- they were included in that sort of organisation for the Croat population in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rajic, are you aware of the fact that this decision about the setting up of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna was arrived at without consulting or without the approval of the legal authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Look, if you're asking about the legal authorities which were set up after the first free democratic elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina, there was no approval of that kind. But if you are asking me whether those were the leftovers of those authorities, in spite of the fact that I did not participate in any of it, I believe that there was not actually any need for a thing like that from those institutions which had de facto ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, we are talking about the bodies which represented Bosnia and Herzegovina on the occasion of it being accepted as a member of the United Nations, and they were the official representation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the eyes of the International Community and in its relations with all the other countries of the world. Do you consider those bodies to be not legal?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know what bodies you're talking about. The Presidency and what else?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Presidency, the General Assembly, the ministries, the government.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I know about the Presidency but I'm not aware of all those other bodies functioning during the war. I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this decision was arrived at without consulting those bodies; is that true?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Without consulting that one particular body, which did exist to -- up to a point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, then. I would like to witness to be shown another document, which we have in the Bosnian and English language. It is from the OJ of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And the Defence has taken the text and the translation from the documents in the case against Martinovic and Naletilic. It was used as a document for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In the transcript there's a certain section that says "cannot distinguish between question and answer." If my learned colleague would please be so polite to again ask the question in order to allow the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last question I put was: Was this decision reached without consulting those bodies? And you replied, "Without consulting that one particular body, which at that time existed." I don't see that there were any other questions, because I moved on to the request for the witness to be shown another document. Is that true, Mr. Rajic? You answered to my question that yes, there was that -- just one body and you meant the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I think. I don't know whether there was any approval. But what I said was that there was no need for approval from such a body. That's my own personal opinion. But as to whether there was any approval, I don't know. I was not involved, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have in front of you the decision of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna dated the 8th of April, 1992 about the setting up of the Croatian Defence Council. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I see here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this decision too was published in the official journal of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna in September 1992. Did you see that decision and was it in line with that decision that the units of the HVO were formed?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I could have seen that decision, and also the other decision, at approximately the same time because I believe that they were published in the same OJ. As to whether I had seen it, prior to that I couldn't have done. I can't remember exactly when I did see it. But if I saw the other one, I would have seen this one too. As to the setting up of the HVO as a military component of the Croat people in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Travnik, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Rajic, that this decision establishes that the Croat Defence Council is set up as the supreme body for the defence of the Croat people, and in Article 2 it is stated that "The Croat Defence Council would take care of the defence of the sovereignty of the area of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna"? Are these provisions that you were aware of when you received the text of that decision?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: I'm aware of that, but I had also said that there were some areas in which Croats got organised and those areas are not referred to in that founding provision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such as, for example, Zenica?

utterances.speaker: TOMISLAV RAJIC
utterances.text: No. Such as, for example, in Zepce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In the beginning of our conversation, we established --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, since this is at the very end, perhaps it would be appropriate for me to ask for this decision to be tendered as evidence and perhaps we could conclude for today. I am probably going to need slightly longer than half an hour tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we keep discovering important text being produced by the Defence. I would like to find out about how you feel about the fact that the first document, which refers to this decision of the 18th of November, 1991, which is translated into English and into French, in its Article 8 indicates that the organisation and the functioning and the relations with other communities are governed by a statute. You've told us just now that this document was something that you found out about at the end of 1992. The Defence then produces a new document which still refers to this decision of the 18th of November, 1991, but the reading of that document shows that the first document of the 18th of November of 1991 was amended on the 3rd of July, 1992. And I no longer find in the text of the articles Article 8, which becomes Article 9, and in Article 9 it is stated that "The internal organisation of that community and its relations with other communities will be organised by separate instruments," in the plural; whereas in the first text it was singular and it was with reference to a statute. Now, this document that you seem to have discovered in 1992, apparently it was amended in July 1992. Did you know that this document had been amended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know. I said when I saw those documents - and I could only see them once they had been published in the OJ - I know nothing about the amendments you've referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then. So you're saying that you discovered them when they were published in the official journal. And it was published at what time, according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see here that it was in September 1992, but you normally don't get the copy on time. The communications were really bad. And we couldn't get it on the same day or even the day after. I suppose it must be appropriate -- and I must have received those documents by the end of the year, the documents you've just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the end of the year. All right, then. So you wanted to tender into evidence the document which was published in the OJ; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. About the setting up of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. So we now need a number and we have to specify that we've got the text in English and in B/C/S. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S version gets the exhibit number DH34; and the English translation gets the exhibit number DH34/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, the best thing to do is to continue tomorrow, so we'll continue at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Witness, unfortunately for you you'll have to spend an extra night in The Hague. So as you know, you no longer have the right to see people between this evening and tomorrow morning. You can't talk to either the Defence or the Prosecution this evening. And do please come back tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you very much. And I'll ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm turning to the Prosecution. So we've got this witness tomorrow plus certainly another one. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right, Mr. President, Your Honours. Can we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem. Partial private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of February, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.08 p.m.,
